title: java tutorial / Creating a source code file
content:
## Creating a source code file

Create a folder for your Java program and open the folder with {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %}. Then in {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %}, create a new file and save it with the name `Hello.java`. When you open that file, the Java Language Server automatically starts loading, and you should see a language status item with a loading icon on the right side of the Status Bar showing the language status is busy. After it finishes loading, you can hover on the language status item and find the loading process has been finished successfully. You can also choose to pin the status item in the status bar.

<video src="images/java-tutorial/JavaHelloWorld.Standalone.mp4" autoplay loop muted playsinline controls title="Creating a source code file">
</video>

>**Note**: If you open a Java file in {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} without opening its folder, the Java Language Server might not work properly.

{% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} will also try to figure out the correct package for the new type and fill the new file from a template. See [Create new file](/docs/java/java-editing.md#create-new-file).

You can also create a Java project using the **Java: Create Java Project** command. Bring up the **Command Palette**  (`kb(workbench.action.showCommands)`) and then type `java` to search for this command. After selecting the command, you will be prompted for the location and name of the project. You can also choose your build tool from this command.

<video src="images/java-tutorial/JavaHelloWorld.Project.mp4" autoplay loop muted playsinline controls title="Create Java Project">
</video>

{% data variables.product.prodname_vscode %} also supports more complex Java projects — see [Project Management](/docs/java/java-project.md).
